questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Career opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: First of all, was it crucial that the country was an English speaking country, but also a place close to home, so my family could visit.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The university's webside could be a bit difficult to navigate, but it was always possible to write to somebody at the university who could answer any question you had.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: If needed it was possible to get the assistance needed upon arrival.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer:
There was different apartments available. Some apartments with 4 people, where you shared two bathrooms and kitchen and livingroom, and some apartments with 6 people where you had your own bathroom and shared livingroom and kitchen. 
There was also the option to living in bigger halls, where there was 12 people living, with private bathroom and sharing two kitchens and two livingrooms

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Some of the hall apartments has a meal plan included in the rent, but the rest had full functional kitchens in the apartments shared with the roommates.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It is a bit pricey, but there is a gym and pool located at the school the students can use.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration for modules where different depending on what you study. For science you got an google questionnaire sent and wrote what modules you would like to register for.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There was advisers available who would help you with any questions you had.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the modules I wished for.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Remember to check when the modules are offered, to avoid any clashes, and remember to check how much outside of class work there is for the module.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: In the later years the modules are very specified, so there is a good opportunity to really learn the materiale

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Most of the teaching was the same as UCPH, with lab work and lectures. There wasn't as many tutorials as there are at UCPH. However, there is more in-class tests, which counts towards the finale grade.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
CCIV10040 - Vikings in the Celtic World
CHEM20080 - Basis of Physical Chemistry
CHEM30090 - Chemistry of Materials
CHEM30110 - Instrumental Analysis
CHEM30200 - Carbonyl Chemistry & Synthesis
CHEM30220 - Mechanism and Stereochemistry

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
CHEM30110 - Instrumental Analysis and CHEM30220 - Mechanism and Stereochemistry were really good courses. Instrumental Analysis is really useful if you wish to work in any chemistry lab or if you need to work with instruments, as you get a good knowledge of how the instruments works. 
Mechanism and Stereochemistry were a good module for getting a good understanding of mechanisms. 
I would also recommend taking a module in a lower level, for getting an easier one, maybe with not to much work, so you have time to explore the country and make friends.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
There are 50 sport clubs and over 70 societies available. 
There are both national and internation sports, and societies for everything.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend joining a sport club or societies, doesn't matter if you have ever played that sport before, as it is a good way to meet people and make friends.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
I would recommend for people to take either a one day trip or weekend trip to explore the country. Cliffs of Moher is a good one day trip, but to go to Northern Ireland, is also a good weekend or day trip. 
A good day trip is also to go see Glendalough, where there is some hiking trips and two lakes, but also some beautiful old ruins from a monastery. 
If you like to hike, then there is some amazing hike tours starting and ending in the city Howth.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It is not very hard to adjust to the local culture.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I would recommend to join a club, it is very cheap and you get to meet new people. Also if you feel comfortable just say hi to somebody in you class, everybody was very welcoming.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Don't know

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Take modules you think sounds fun, even if they don't match your degree. You have a good opportunity to take modules which they don't offer any other places int he world. 
Join a club or a society. It is a very cheap and a great way to meet people and make friends. Don't be afraid to join if you are only there for a semester, they are used to that and are just happy to get some members and friends. 
Don't forget to enjoy it. It is easy to stress about assignments and schoolwork, but remember you are there to meet know people and learn about a different culture than your own.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Remember to bring some warm clothes, as there can be very cold on campus and during lectures.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: To know that it was possible for me to go to a new culture and live and study there

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The amount of work for some of modules were pretty high, and covid. There was a lot of corona cases in Ireland during finals, which added a layer of stress about the finals and if it was possible for me to get home

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
